incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1, arts. 4 (application), 9 (incorporation), 10 (contents of articles), 11 (certificate of incorporation), 20 (name), 22 (registered office), 196 (directors); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, C.Q.L.R. c. P-44.1, arts. 8, 11 and 22.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), 400 boulevard Jean-Lesage, Quebec, QC; online portal: www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution / Articles of Incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The company may be incorporated with one or more common shares without par value issued for consideration fixed by the board. There is no statutory escrow account rule; subscription funds must be paid and credited before share certificates are delivered. If shares are issued for property, a plan of assets and liabilities must be attached.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME]: The Board resolves: (1) the subscription agreements for common shares are accepted, and share certificates will be issued after the stated contribution is paid into the corporate trust account; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], Montreal, Quebec, and the Enterprise Registrar is designated as the address for service; (3) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, [Name] Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board with usual powers; (4) the officers are authorized to execute banking resolutions, pay incorporation fees, and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Legal Form Verification and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online registration services (NUANS name search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a NUANS name search through the REQ/Canadian trademark database. Verify that the proposed corporate name is distinctive, lawful, not confusing with existing names, and contains an appropriate legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.'. Submit a name reservation request through the REQ online portal or in writing. If approved, retain the reservation number, which is valid for 90 days for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with legal element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusion or similarity, file a revised name reservation with a new distinctive element or a geographic qualifier, or obtain the written consent of the conflicting name holder before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Signature and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Electronic Incorporation (Constitution en ligne)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory articles of incorporation including the corporate name, registered office address, authorized share structure, restrictions on share transfers, and the number of directors. The incorporator(s) must sign the articles electronically or manually; each director must provide a signed consent to act. File the completed articles through the REQ online platform, pay the applicable registration fee, and retain the electronic filing receipt. If the subscription consideration includes property, attach a plan of assets and liabilities.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each founding director
NUANS name reservation number and report
Original plan of assets and liabilities (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ queries the articles, submit a formal written response in the REQ electronic file, or file amended articles if a correction is required. In case of registry error, request administrative rectification under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Register of Enterprises (RENE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the articles, confirm the issuance of the certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution) and the company's nine-digit Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Download the official electronic extract from the enterprise register. This extract is the conclusive proof of corporate existence for opening bank accounts and registering with tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register extract contains discrepancies in the corporate name, registered office, or directors, file a correction declaration with REQ supported by the certificate of incorporation and other corroborating documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Governance Resolutions and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate governance; subsequent notice to Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) via update declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or adopt a written resolution of the first board of directors. Approve the articles and by-laws, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, elect officers, accept share subscriptions, and fix the registered office. After the meeting, file the required enterprise register update declaration with REQ within 30 days to record the appointment of officers and directors and to confirm the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Mutual consent forms for individual officers
REQ declaration de mise à jour
Minutes of the organizational board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects the update declaration due to incomplete director or officer information, correct and resubmit the declaration through the REQ online portal; administrative cure may be available if filed within the statutory 30-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certificate of incorporation and NEQ, obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA and complete the Quebec enterprise file with Revenu Québec. Register for corporate income tax, GST/HST/QST accounts, payroll deduction accounts, and any required digital economy vendor registration. Confirm the place-of-supply rules for digital webtoon subscriptions sold through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, and file any QST remittance registrations in accordance with the Quebec Tax Administration Act.
required_dossiers: First board resolution on banking and officers
Bank account details for tax remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec delays or mismatches the accounts, verify that the federal BN and Quebec CLÉ number are linked; if necessary, submit a formal account linkage request and provide the enterprise register extract to enable reconciliation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to digital webtoon publishing; if a physical office or studio is established, the local municipal permits office is the relevant authority for occupancy and zoning clearances.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; no municipal or provincial operating licence is mandated for remote digital publishing. An optional occupancy permit may be required for a leased physical office addressed to Service de l’urbanisme et du développement économique of the relevant Quebec municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required because digital webtoon publishing creates no physical project and no regulated contaminating discharge under the Environment Quality Act, C.Q.L.R. c. Q-2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater, VOC, or industrial solid waste standards. If an ordinary office is leased, municipal waste and sewer by-laws apply to routine office waste; electronic waste from IT equipment is governed by the Quebec regulation respecting the recovery of electrical and electronic equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil defense or fire safety certificate is required for a pure digital publishing operation. If a physical office is leased, the lessee must comply with the Quebec Building Code for fire safety, exits, and public occupancy requirements, and with CNESST workplace health and safety rules for employees. A fire safety inspection report may be requested by the landlord or property insurer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes and Revenu Québec for provincial taxes; portals at canada.ca/cra and revenuquebec.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations obtain Business Number (BN) from CRA upon incorporation via online application; foreign entities register for BN through CRA portal or Canadian representative; Quebec entities register separately with Revenu Québec for QST; BN serves as primary TIN
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; classification determined by federal or provincial incorporation status under Income Tax Act; hybrid mismatch rules apply without elective mechanisms

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST (Goods and Services Tax / Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST registrants transmit electronic data under Excise Tax Act; Revenu Québec mandates digital invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API requirements, and digital stamping for qualifying transactions

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST/QST if exported within prescribed timelines and documented; offshore services qualify under non-resident recipient and performance conditions
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims incur penalties up to 200% of tax, interest, and criminal prosecution; retrospective clawbacks under Excise Tax Act section 285

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing routine capital controls. The Department of Finance Canada administers relevant sanctions and certain financial-sector policies; FINTRAC administers federal anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing compliance requirements. Quebec does not maintain a separate general foreign-exchange control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering requirements, tax rules, securities laws, and bank compliance review. There is no general exchange-control approval requirement for foreign investment, intercompany funding, payment of dividends, or repatriation of capital. A Canadian corporation may remit dividends or other lawful distributions to non-residents after satisfying corporate-law solvency requirements, applicable withholding tax, treaty eligibility and documentation, and any applicable tax-clearance or reporting obligations. Interest, royalties, service fees, and other cross-border payments require appropriate contractual and transfer-pricing support and may attract Canadian withholding tax, generally subject to treaty reduction where available. Payments to related non-residents may also require transfer-pricing documentation and information returns. Banks may request source-of-funds, beneficial-ownership, transaction-purpose, and underlying-contract evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated to Canada and no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio for export receipts. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency or offshore, subject to tax, accounting, sanctions, contractual, and reporting requirements. Financial institutions may request invoices, platform settlement statements, distribution agreements, or other evidence supporting the nature and origin of incoming funds. Foreign affiliate, foreign-property, and international transaction reporting may apply depending on ownership, balances, and transaction facts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment and collection services; not a substitute for a Canadian deposit-taking institution account where the corporation requires a conventional Canadian operating account, deposit protection, or local credit facilities. Availability, CAD collection details, safeguarding model, permitted business activities, and cross-border transfer limits depend on the provider's Canadian authorization, product terms, and the corporation's residence and ownership profile. Offshore e-money institution accounts do not remove Canadian AML, tax, sanctions, or books-and-records obligations. Confirm that the provider accepts Canadian corporations and the digital-content business model before relying on it for platform settlements or material treasury balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statute requires directors to attend a bank branch in person. Canadian banks set their own onboarding procedures and may permit remote applications, electronic signatures, and video verification for eligible resident corporations. A non-resident-owned corporation, foreign directors, complex ownership, or higher-risk cross-border activity can trigger enhanced verification, certified or notarized documents, a live interview, or an in-person appointment. Requirements differ by bank and product; confirm the bank's current Quebec onboarding rules before incorporation or funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, layered foreign holding companies, or missing control-person information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles and corporate registry extract; ownership chart through all intermediate entities to natural-person beneficial owners; shareholder and director registers; identification and address evidence for directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners; trust or nominee instruments where applicable; corporate resolutions; and explanations of any ownership or control complexity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership, foreign directors, or remote onboarding that prevents routine identity verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified incorporation and good-standing records; constitutional documents; passports and proof of residential address; certified translations where required; Canadian business address and operational evidence; board authorization for account opening; tax identification details; and completion of the bank's identity-verification or interview process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or irregular initial capital transfers, third-party funding, or transfers inconsistent with stated business scale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan documents; board approvals; sender bank statements or other source-of-funds evidence; sender ownership information; wire instructions matching the documented investor or lender; capitalization table; and a concise explanation of the transfer's purpose and expected use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-currency receipts from app stores, payment processors, distributors, or foreign counterparties that do not match the stated publishing business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google developer or publisher agreements; platform account ownership evidence; distribution and syndication contracts; invoices or royalty statements; settlement reports; customer geography and currency summaries; website or application details; and reconciliation from gross sales through platform fees, refunds, taxes, and net deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, opaque intermediaries, or counterparties with unexplained links to restricted territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identification and beneficial-ownership information; contract, invoice, and delivery evidence; payment-chain details; documented sanctions screening; explanation of any geographic nexus; and evidence that the transaction is permitted under applicable Canadian sanctions and other relevant laws. Do not process a transaction while a sanctions prohibition or unresolved match remains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party royalties, licensing fees, management charges, or intercompany balances without commercial support.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany agreements; evidence of rights ownership and services performed; pricing methodology and transfer-pricing support; invoices and payment calculations; withholding-tax analysis and forms; and required Canadian tax filings or information returns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscriptions and shareholder loans from an account in the documented investor's or lender's name to the corporation's Canadian business account, preferably by bank-to-bank SWIFT transfer for material amounts. Provide the receiving bank with the subscription or loan agreement, corporate resolution, ownership records, source-of-funds evidence, sender details, and a clear payment narrative such as equity subscription or shareholder loan. Canada does not prescribe a universal foreign-exchange purpose code for these transfers; use the bank's requested transaction-purpose classification accurately and do not characterize debt as equity or vice versa. Reconcile the receipt to the corporate ledger and retain wire confirmations. Assess withholding tax, transfer pricing, thin-capitalization rules, and any applicable international information returns for related-party financing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's equivalent cross-border payment instruction for ordinary supplier, licensing, royalty, and service payments. Match beneficiary details, invoice, contract, currency, and payment reference; retain approval and accounting records. Commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, and bank guarantees may be used where transaction value or counterparty risk justifies them, subject to bank credit approval and documentary terms. Verify sanctions, withholding tax, treaty documentation, transfer-pricing support, and invoice authenticity before payment. App-store and payment-processor settlements should be reconciled to platform statements, fees, refunds, and chargebacks. The applicable rail and settlement timing depend on the banks, currencies, correspondent banks, and contract terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian bank or other appropriately authorized counterparty, subject to documentation, suitability, credit approval, and the bank's requirements for an underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered and appropriate for a restricted or non-deliverable currency exposure; Canadian-dollar exposures generally have accessible deliverable markets, so an NDF should not be assumed to be necessary or available for every currency.

Currency swaps, including cross-currency swaps, for documented financing or recurring cash-flow exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, master documentation, collateral terms, and applicable derivatives reporting or conduct requirements.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for conversion of receipts and payment funding, with transaction approvals and accounting records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration Annuelle) of Enterprise Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: filed annually on or before the anniversary date of the enterprise registration; the Registraire issues a reminder notice at least 60 days before the filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a monetary penalty of approximately CAD 600 plus administrative collection costs; continued non-filing for 24 consecutive months permits administrative dissolution by the Registraire after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return (applicable only if the corporation is a federal business corporation, i.e., incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuance; not based on the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for three consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by the Director of Corporations Canada under section 235 CBCA after prior notice; directors and officers remain liable for corporate obligations until dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Audit and Minute Book Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate registered office holdings; internal governance requirement — no government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in advance of the annual shareholder meeting and in any event within 15 months of the previous annual meeting; update immediately upon any share transfer, director appointment, or registered office change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers may be personally liable for inaccurate, incomplete, or untraceable statutory records; missing or defective registers may invalidate evidentiary presumptions in litigation and cause administrative delays with regulators.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting Resolution Records and AGM Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book; internal governance record — no government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held not later than 18 months after incorporation and thereafter within 15 months after the preceding AGM; minutes must be inserted in the minute book and signed by the chair within a reasonable time.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with CBCA/Quebec Business Corporations Act AGM deadlines may permit shareholders to apply for court intervention; persistent failure creates a basis for administrative compliance notices and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a non-publicly listed private business corporation engaged in digital webtoon publishing under federal CBCA or Quebec Business Corporations Act; mandatory independent audit arises only if the corporation is a reporting issuer, is subject to an audit requirement under another statute, or if shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting shares requisition an audit; otherwise, private corporations may adopt an annual waiver resolution to dispense with the audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) for Canadian private business corporations; internal full accrual accounting is required for annual corporate tax filings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec requires every enterprise registered with the Registraire des entreprises to establish and maintain a register of ultimate beneficiaries and to update it within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change; the annual declaration further confirms the accuracy of ultimate beneficiary information on the public registry. If the corporation is a federal CBCA corporation, the register of individuals with significant control must be maintained and updated within 15 days of any transfer of significant control, with annual confirmation via the federal annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control / Ultimate Beneficiaries

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200 – $600 USD per year for registered office and corporate filing agent services in Quebec, depending on service scope and monthly volume
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,700 – $11,100 USD per year for a certified independent audit of a small digital-content publishing private corporation, depending on transaction count, intercompany payments, and multi-jurisdictional app revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate of 26.5% (federal Part I general rate of 15.0% after the 38.0% basic rate less the 10.0% provincial abatement and the 13.0% general rate reduction; Quebec general rate of 11.5% under the Taxation Act, R.S.Q. c. I-3). This 26.5% headline applies to the webtoon subscription, chapter unlocking, and licensing revenue unless the corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the small business deduction.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD): a qualified CCPC pays a combined 12.2% (federal 9.0% + Quebec 3.2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, prorated for a short taxation year and across associated corporations. Quebec's refundable tax credits for multimedia titles and for electronic business development may reduce the effective rate on eligible webtoon-production labour; the R&D investment tax credit (federal 20% non-refundable / 35% refundable for small CCPCs, plus the Quebec SR&ED credit) is available for qualifying software development. These incentives are subject to the anti-avoidance condition that the underlying activities and wages are actually incurred, paid, and retained in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Corporation Internet Filing service using CRA-certified tax software; mandatory e-filing applies to corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000 for the taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one T2 return per fiscal period, normally not exceeding 53 weeks; no split-year election is available for a business corporation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due no later than six months after the fiscal period end. The balance of federal tax is due two months after year-end, or three months for a CCPC entitled to the SBD. Instalments are generally required when federal and provincial combined tax exceeds CAD 3,000, payable monthly or quarterly in advance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from webtoon chapter unlocking, subscriptions, digital advertising, licensing, syndication, and any ancillary merchandise or fan-support revenue, gross of channel fees charged by Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue from a Canadian business carried on by the taxpayer. A non-resident-controlled Quebec corporation must include all gross proceeds attributable to its Canadian permanent establishment; platform commissions are deductible as selling expenses only if supported by contractual invoices and actually borne by the entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: aggregate of business, property, and taxable capital gains less deductible loss carry-forwards, donations, and other deductions; mandatory transfer pricing adjustments under ITA s.247(2) are reflected in the income computation and are not merely a disclosure schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned Canadian webtoon corporation reports only Canadian-source business income; foreign-source royalties are excluded unless effectively connected to the Canadian business. The return must be filed in Canadian dollars using CRA-accepted foreign exchange rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic Part I tax calculated by applying the 38.0% basic rate, the 10.0% federal abatement, the 13.0% general rate reduction, the 9.0% SBD rate, and any investment tax credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled by a non-resident cannot claim the SBD; the general 15.0% federal rate applies. The foreign parent must not report this entity's income in its own return unless the Quebec corporation is a branch or a sham.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim non-capital losses incurred in the webtoon startup phase, carried back three years (via s.164(2)) and forward up to 20 taxation years, subject to the continuity-of-business rules on change of control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are preserved only where the same entity carries on the business in Canada; a transfer of the digital publishing business to a non-resident affiliate extinguishes the loss. A loss generated in a Quebec subsidiary cannot be transferred to a US parent under group relief rules, because Canada does not permit consolidated filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part XIII / NR4 remittance (outside the T2 body)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information return and remittance for dividends or amounts under Part XIII paid or credited to non-residents; this is a mandatory compliance complement to the T2 required for any shareholder distribution to a foreign owner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold 25% statutory Part XIII tax, or the treaty rate where Form NR301 and a valid certificate of residence are retained; remit the amount to CRA by the 15th day of the month following the payment; issue NR4 slips to the non-resident payee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months under ITA s.162(1), increased to 10% for a second offence within three years under s.162(2); gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under s.163(2); daily compound interest at the prescribed rate; criminal prosecution under s.239 for wilful evasion carries fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years.
